# Cutaway critique, round 2

**Page:** `docs/lab/cutaway.html` (drawings `docs/assets/svg/cutaway.svg` and `cutaway-simple.svg`, generated by `docs/assets/svg/src/cutaway.mjs`; behaviour in `docs/lab/cutaway.js`)
**Viewports:** 1440×900 (DPR 2) and 390×844 (DPR 3, touch). Every capture was taken at least 2.5 s after load, once the draw-in had finished.
**Reviewer stance:** a principal illustrator who grew up on classic aviation cutaway posters. I came to this with fresh eyes and checked it against the round-1 list.

## What changed since round 1 (verified)

- Torn-skin cut edges in copper, with hatched section faces at the wing root and on the nacelle. This is the biggest improvement: it now reads as a cutaway and not an outline.
- Line weight now has tiers. The silhouette is clearly heavier than the interior, and the far-side lines fade.
- Systems runs are drawn. Hover lights the part's run (for example, part 17 lights the hydraulic run from the gear to the tail).
- The engine has a fan face, an opened core and a cut nacelle. The cut wing panel shows ribs. The cabin has floor and cargo-hold boxes.
- Callout names are set in IBM Plex Mono. The numbers run in order clockwise from the cabin top. The title block uses generic figures (36.8 m / 33.9 m / 11.9 m).
- Card: compact 2×2 facts grid, "+2 flags" chip, correct singular and plural, docked at a fixed position in the top-left. It is 255–335 px tall and never runs below the fold.
- Focus bug fixed. Tab from 26 goes to "Back to the workspace" and the card hides cleanly. Shift+Tab returns to 26. The card link has `tabindex=-1` while the card is not pinned, and Enter/Space on a part opens the page.
- Phone: zoned list with copper-tick headers, rows 48 px tall, a numbered dot on every part, a 2.5× zoom inset of the selected part, a phone-specific lede, the sticky figure, and no horizontal scroll (scrollWidth 390).

## Interaction test results

- **Hover on a part or a label:** works. Other parts dim, the active tag fills teal, the system run lights, and the connector draws.
- **Card position:** always docks top-left over the title block and legend (318 px wide). It never covers the active part. **But the connector runs from the card's right edge straight to the part.** For parts 17 and 20 that teal line cuts diagonally across the whole fuselage, about 1,100 px long. It is the loudest line on the sheet, and it is not part of the drawing.
- **Keyboard:** tab order runs 01 → 26 and then leaves the SVG. The aria-labels are good. Escape hides the card. Pass.
- **Click → part page:** clicking part 03 goes to `index.html#/parts?pn=GN-28-R010`. Clicking label 03 goes to the same URL. Pass.
- **Phone list:** 26 disclosure rows. Opening a row puts a ring on the drawing, shows the inset and scrolls the row to just below the sticky figure (row top 206 px, figure bottom 194 px). Tapping dot 20 on the drawing opens row 20 and scrolls to it. Pass.
  - Dot hit targets measure **31×31 px**, below the 44 px target.
  - Number badges overlap in the nose cluster (11/07, 12/09) and at 22/24.
  - When a row opens, its zone header sits hidden under the sticky figure.
  - The inset frame butts against the top edge of the figure and is clipped there.
- **Console:** no errors.
- **Flake:** in 1 of about 10 phone loads, `.cw-mfig` was missing straight after `data-ready`. I could not reproduce it in 8 dedicated reloads, so note it but don't chase it. Possible cause: `render()` being called again while `loadSVG` is still in flight.

## Originality check

- The drawing is built from code (procedural 3-D geometry in `cutaway.mjs`). The line quality is uniform in the way generated geometry is, not in the way a trace is. The shape is a generic low-wing twin with winglets and a conventional tail.
- A grep for Airbus, Boeing, A32x, Embraer, CFM, LEAP, Pratt, Rolls and livery found nothing. The only "737" hits are path coordinates. All SVG text is generic: part names, the title block, "GENERIC NARROWBODY · SCHEMATIC — NOT ENGINEERING DATA · NTS". All part numbers are fictional `GN-` numbers.
- The dimensions are now generic (36.8 m / 33.9 m / 11.9 m). **Clearly original.**

## Scores (1–5)

| Criterion | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Craft** | **3.0** | Real progress: weighted silhouette, torn copper edges, hatched section faces, a coherent 3-D projection. Still wrong or weak: <br>• The main gear (17/18) sits directly behind the engine on a vertical post, not inboard of the nacelle under the wing root. <br>• There is no visible pylon: the nacelle hangs from a single curve. <br>• The engine core reads as a coil spring (a helix), not as stage discs. <br>• The wing, fin and tailplanes are still single flat outlines with no thickness or closed tips. <br>• The far tailplane is two loose lines. <br>• The cabin interior is a mass of same-weight boxes that turns to moiré in the mid-body. |
| **Detail** | **3.0** | Systems runs, cargo boxes, wing ribs, an opened engine, a nose gear with a strut, and a radome with the radar. Missing or unreadable: <br>• wing spars and the centre wing box; <br>• floor beams that read as beams; <br>• flight-deck furniture; <br>• doors; <br>• a main-gear bay. <br>Parts are still primitive glyphs (boxes and cylinders), so no pump reads as a pump. The tail is sparse: four parts, no APU body, no rear spar or bulkhead structure. |
| **Legibility** | **3.5** | Mono names at about 13 px with tidy tags, and the whole sheet fits above the fold. Against that: <br>• The **SPAN 33.9 m** dimension runs diagonally from the far wingtip, high on the left (its stray arrow sits in empty space by the title block), to the near wingtip. It crosses the fuselage and about 6 leaders. <br>• The **LENGTH** label sits on top of nose wheel 13. <br>• The left column reads 04, 06, 07, 08… with 05 floating to the right, and leaders 04–07 cross one another in the nose. <br>• Leaders 01–03 and 25–26 still drop 300–450 px through the cut. <br>• The card connector (see above) cuts across the drawing. <br>• Phone badges collide in the nose. |
| **Brand fit** | **4.5** | Strong. #09131F field, titanium ghost structure, glowing teal parts with a halo, copper cut edges and hatching, a Plex Mono title block with a copper tick, a teal-on-navy card, copper zone ticks on the phone. Small deductions: the card uses Inter for the fact values (fine), and the copper hatching is very thin at 1×. |
| **Would a cutaway-poster fan admire it?** | **3.0** | They would now recognise it as a cutaway and enjoy the peeled skin and the lit system runs. The gear sitting behind the engine and the coil-spring engine would still be spotted in seconds. The interior lacks the dense, confident structure (spars, beams, frames at rhythm) and the depth gradient that make a poster worth staring at. |

**Mean: (3.0 + 3.0 + 3.5 + 4.5 + 3.0) / 5 = 3.4** (up from 3.0 in round 1)

## Top 6 remaining improvements (priority order)

### 1. Fix the main gear, pylon and engine anatomy (cutaway.mjs)
- **Main gear:** move parts 17 (carbon brake) and 18 (main wheel) **inboard of the nacelle**. Put the axle at about 0.55 of the root chord from the root leading edge and about 2.5 m from the centreline. On this drawing that is roughly halfway between the fuselage belly and the inboard face of the nacelle, under the wing root. Draw the leg from the rear spar down to the axle, with a side brace from the leg's mid-point to the belly. Add a wheel-well outline in the belly, plus the far gear at ghost opacity.
- **Pylon:** a swept box from the top of the nacelle, front to back, up to the lower surface of the wing. Use four edges at tier T3 plus an aft fairing curve. Parts 14, 15 and 16 must sit on or inside it.
- **Engine core:** replace the helix with 6–8 discrete compressor discs (ellipses spaced along the axis, getting smaller towards the back). Add a combustor ring (a thicker ellipse), 2–3 turbine discs and a tail cone. The coil-spring look is the single most "wrong" read on the sheet.

### 2. Rebuild the dimensioning and the card connector so no auxiliary line crosses the aircraft
- **SPAN:** delete the diagonal. Draw it as a straight dimension in the empty bottom-right band, between projection lines dropped from both wingtips. Or show only the near semi-span along the near wing's trailing edge, labelled "½ SPAN 16.95 m".
- **LENGTH:** move it below the bottom callout row, or run it 40 units under the belly with extension lines from the nose tip and the tail cone. Keep its label clear of nose wheel 13.
- **Connector:** route it in two segments only, and never through the fuselage. Go from the card's nearest edge to the active part's **own leader tag**, then let the existing leader (which lights teal) finish the path. In practice: draw the connector to the tag's outer edge (a horizontal-then-vertical elbow in the margin), or drop it altogether and just glow the active leader plus tag. The card already sits in a fixed corner, so the leader is the link.

### 3. Re-lay the left and top callouts: numeric order on each side, no crossings, short leaders
- Put **05** in the left column, in order (04, 05, 06, 07…). Sort the column by each part's projected y so leaders fan out without crossing. Today 04's leader crosses 06 and 07.
- Move **01–03** (cabin and pack bay) to the bottom row under the wing root, and **25–26** to the right column, below 24. Their leaders then run 120–200 units instead of dropping 300–450 px through the cut.
- Cap leader length at 320 units. Use one angled segment plus one horizontal run. Put a 3-unit #09131F halo on every leader where it crosses structure (already there; make sure it is applied to the new routes).

### 4. Give the airframe thickness and structural rhythm where the eye lands
- Wing: draw upper and lower surface lines with t/c ≈ 0.11 at the root and 0.09 at the tip, close the tip, and add the front and rear spars (T3, 0.9) running the length of the cut panel, with ribs every ~1.2 m between them. Do the same for the fin (a rudder hinge line plus a closed tip) and both tailplanes. Join the far tailplane into a closed outline.
- Fuselage: show frames at **every 4th station at T3** and the rest at T4, so the barrel gets a beat. Show floor beams as a visible ladder (T3), and a keel beam.
- Mid-body: cull the far-half cabin boxes and drop the near-half seat boxes to T4 at 0.18 opacity. This removes the moiré and lets the systems runs and parts read.
- Add a centre wing box at the wing root, under the floor (front and rear spar, 3 ribs). Part 03 (fuel boost pump) then sits in its tank.

### 5. Make the parts read as objects, not primitives
- **Pumps (03, 14):** a cylinder plus a flange disc plus two port stubs.
- **Valves (01, 15):** a butterfly body (a short cylinder) plus a square actuator box on top.
- **LRUs (04–07, 10, 11):** a box with a front-panel handle line and a connector strip, sitting in a two-shelf **avionics rack** drawn under the flight deck.
- **Servos (20, 21, 23):** a cylinder plus a rod plus a clevis.
- **Wheel and brake (17, 18):** tyre torus plus hub plus a stack of 5 brake discs.
- **APU (22, 24):** draw a small APU body (a cylinder with an exhaust cone) in the tail cone, then mount 22 and 24 on it. Add the aft pressure bulkhead as a dome at T3.
- Keep the glow and halo. Aim for 2–4 extra strokes per glyph.

### 6. Phone polish: tap targets, badge collisions, header context, inset clipping
- Raise `.cw-ndot-hit` to **44×44 CSS px**. Today they measure 31 px, because the radius is set in viewBox units that scale down. Compute the radius from `44 / (svg.clientWidth / viewBox.width) / 2`.
- Fix badge collisions with a small relaxation pass in the generator. Push overlapping dots apart along the leader direction until there is at least a 2-unit gap, and draw a 0.6-weight tick back to the part. This affects 11/07, 12/09 and 22/24.
- Give the sticky figure a zone caption strip (Plex Mono 11 px, copper tick) along its bottom edge, showing the open row's zone. The zone header otherwise sits hidden under the figure.
- Inset the zoom box by 12 units from the figure's top-left (IX = IY = 22). Give it a 1-unit #09131F outer stroke so it is not clipped by the figure border.
- Make the phone drawing taller. It is 194 px of a 358 px width today. Crop the viewBox tighter around the fuselage (≈1000×470), or flatten the camera about 6°. Bring back the T3 frames at 0.35 opacity so it reads as a cutaway and not an icon.

## What already works (keep it)
- The torn copper cut edges and hatched section faces. The lit system runs on hover. The full poster fitting above the fold at 1440×900.
- The compact docked card with the 2×2 facts, the singular/plural fix and the "+N flags" chip.
- The keyboard model: numeric tab order, a clean exit after 26, Escape, Enter → part page.
- The phone pattern: zoned disclosure list, sticky figure, ring plus 2.5× inset, tap-on-drawing → open row.
- Originality: procedural geometry, generic figures, no names or liveries.
